name: Guinea
headline: Guinea: +6.9% growth in 2025, 3.1% inflation, debt 36% of GDP
sections: Guinea is a $42.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 105th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $4,935 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.7% of GDP (2022).

Consumer prices rose 3.1% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 10.5% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.2% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 7.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 36% of GDP (2025), a low level that has risen from 29% in 2020. The general government balance is −6.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −14.7% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 104% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 27.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 20% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 60.9 years (2024). Population: 15.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
